fields.id: namespace:path usable as '/place template <id> x y z [rotation] [mirror]' (origin = template's min corner)
fields.bottom_layer_summary: top 3 block ids (by count) in the y=0 layer, their counts, and is_foundation_course (true = dirt/stone/terrain course meant to be buried, false = walkable floor material)
fields.palette_top: top 6 non-air blocks in the whole structure by block count
fields.has_roof: true if any stair/slab/wall/trapdoor block appears in the top third of the structure's height
fields.entities: entity ids baked into the structure (e.g. item frames), if any
fields.notes: human-readable classification: role, standalone-vs-fragment status for tavern/ruin pieces, hearth contents for ruins
fields.recommended_y_offset: 0 if the bottom layer is a walkable floor, -1 if it's a foundation/dirt course to bury
fields.palette_size: distinct block states in the palette (extra)
fields.has_campfire / has_furnace / has_chest /: literal block-presence flags (extra, used to find ruin hearths and identify jigsaw fragments)
fields.standalone: present only on nova_structures tavern/ruin_town/wild_ruin records — true if the piece has walls+roof+floor and can be hand-placed alone, false if it's a jigsaw fragment meant to be assembled procedurally

inn.why: tavern_house_<wood> is the only STANDALONE tavern piece in the set (walls+roof+floor, ~1450-1480 blocks, ~18x13x20) — tavern_enterance_* and tavern_middle_* are jigsaw fragments for the mod's own procedural multi-floor generation and are not meant to stand alone. Spruce/snowy wood reads closest to the meadow_swiss chalet palette (spruce_planks + dark_oak + white accents); oak/dark_oak are the next-closest matches.

mill.why: A literal windmill (18x26x17, oak_log/spruce/stripped_oak_log/spruce_stairs palette) from the Towns and Towers sunflower_plains_farm set. It is outside the approved meadow_swiss/classic style pair, but its wood palette reads generically Swiss/rustic and it is the only real windmill available across the installed template packs — far better than a procedural mill_race/mill_roof box. Flag for Josh's sign-off since it's a cross-set borrow.

cottages_2.why: Both are compact roofed meadow_swiss chalets (9x10x9, 810 blocks), visually identical style but distinct footprints/interiors — good as two named characters' homes.

square_centre.why: meadow_meeting_point_1 is an open 11x5x11 plaza (walkable floor, y offset 0) — place the classic well (well_bottom then well_top stacked on top) at its center. No standalone well exists in meadow_swiss, so this is the intended classic-fallback pairing.

granary_barn.why: GAP: neither meadow_swiss nor classic has a dedicated barn/granary. rustic_barn_professions_1 (11x14x10, spruce_planks + brick trim) is the closest style match found anywhere in the installed packs — cross-set borrow, needs Josh's sign-off. classic_large_farm_1 is a same-style fallback but is an open crop plot, not an enclosed barn — would need a custom roofed shed built over it to read as a granary.

store.why: No dedicated 'shop' piece in the approved sets. classic_small_house_1/2 (6x6x6) are small enough to dress as a general store; a nova_structures trader_car piece (small market-cart decoration, snowy/spruce variant) can be placed outside as a stall front for extra readability.

library_or_church.why: meadow_swiss has no standalone library (only a combined cartographer_and_library) and no church at all — classic_library_1 (8x9x11) and classic_church_1 (10x12x7, cobblestone chapel with a ladder to the bell level) are the exact style-guide fallback picks named in the brief. Pick one per the Works/story need, or use both if the valley wants a chapel and a library as separate buildings.

bell_tower.why: GAP: no dedicated bell/watch tower exists in meadow_swiss or classic (outpost/towers/meadow/base_plate.nbt is a jigsaw foundation-only piece with no static tower body available to hand-place). meadow_temple_1 is the tallest roofed meadow_swiss building (14 high) and reads as a landmark/civic structure — best available stand-in. classic_church_1's ladder-to-roof level is the next option if a literal bell perch is wanted.

town_hall.why: The single largest meadow_swiss building (17x12x13, 2652 blocks, full pitched roof) — no dedicated 'town hall' piece exists in either set, so the largest/most ornamented house is the natural civic-building stand-in.

newcomer_houses_3.why: Five distinct medium meadow_swiss house variants (9-12 wide, 10 tall, 1170-1560 blocks) exist — enough to give Bram, Marnie and Pip visibly different homes with two more variants in reserve.

greenhouse.why: GAP: no glass-roofed/greenhouse structure exists anywhere in the installed meadow_swiss, classic, or nova_structures packs. Recommend a small custom build (glass-pane walls + light-blue stained glass roof over a meadow_swiss-scale footprint, using the same spruce/dark_oak trim as the houses) rather than forcing a mismatched template — flag for Josh's design call.

bathhouse.why: GAP: same as greenhouse — no bathhouse/spa piece exists in the installed packs. Recommend repurposing classic_medium_house_1 or classic_medium_house_2 (small, roofless utility footprints, 210-252 blocks) as the shell and dressing the interior with a wooden tub + cauldron custom-built in kubejs, or a fully custom small structure — flag for Josh's design call.

starting_ruin.why: wild_ruin pieces are standalone (self-contained, no jigsaw partner needed) unlike ruin_town pieces (built for procedural town assembly). wild_ruin_23 (10x11x9, 952 blocks) already contains a furnace — a ready-made hearth spot to swap for the story's hearthstone. wild_ruin_15 (5x7x5) already has a campfire if a smaller ruin is wanted; wild_ruin_29 (7x7x10) also has a furnace. None of the 103 ruin_town pieces contain a campfire or furnace, so wild_ruin is the right pool for 'needs a spot for a hearthstone'.

works_interior_rooms.why: 59 bunker pieces cover the full kit needed for a sealed underground Works: an entrance room, hallway segments (16 variants) to route between rooms, five room sizes (5x5 / small / medium / big / largest / triple-bay / cylinder) to vary chamber shapes, and stairs/ladder pieces to change levels. All are interior-only (no exterior wall/roof) so they slot inside the existing sealed shell.
